Absolute value is distance from zero. The absolute value of five is five. The absolute value of negative five is also five. Distance is never negative.
Think of it as distance from home. You can be five blocks east or five blocks west. Either way, you're five blocks from home.
So the absolute value of x minus a equals b means x is b away from a, in either direction. That's why you always write two equations.
Solve the absolute value of x minus three equals five. Five above three is eight. Five below three is negative two.
Write it as two equations. x minus three equals five gives eight. x minus three equals negative five gives negative two. Two answers.
Trap alert. If you only said eight, you missed the other side. Check negative two: negative two minus three is negative five, and its absolute value is five. It works.
What if the absolute value equals a negative number? Distance can't be negative. So there's no solution.
And if it equals zero, there's only one answer. Zero has no other side.
Let's try an SAT style question. A temperature t stays within two degrees of seventy. Which inequality shows this?
Distance from seventy is the absolute value of t minus seventy. Within two means at most two. So the absolute value of t minus seventy is less than or equal to two.
Trap alert. Greater than or equal to two means at least two away. Eighty would fit, but it's ten degrees away. That's not within two.
